comments.note: outVscode and outClaudeCode are kept as required fields (not optional) even though @deprecated. Making them optional now would break persona-builder.ts line 328 (outputDir = target === 'vscode' ? suiteConfig.outVscode : suiteConfig.outClaudeCode) which assigns the value to path.join() expecting a string. A follow-up WP should make them optional simultaneously with updating the builder's output-dir resolution logic to read from outputDirs first.

frontmatter.ts resolveFrontmatterTemplate still falls back to DEFAULT_FRONTMATTER_VSCODE for unknown targets (line: return target === 'vscode' ? DEFAULT_FRONTMATTER_VSCODE : DEFAULT_FRONTMATTER_CLAUDE_CODE). Now that targets can be arbitrary strings, this fallback will silently return the Claude Code template for custom targets. A follow-up WP using TargetRegistry should look up defaultFrontmatter from the registry instead.
No observations that block this WP — code in touched files is clean and consistent with the project's layered architecture.

comments.note: outputDirs in SuiteConfig (src/plugins/types.ts) is typed and documented via @deprecated JSDoc on outVscode/outClaudeCode, but the runtime at persona-builder.ts:328 still reads `target === 'vscode' ? suiteConfig.outVscode : suiteConfig.outClaudeCode`. outputBasename resolution (persona-builder.ts lines 332–338) uses hard-coded string comparisons ('vscode', 'claude-code') for vs_file_name/cc_file_name context fields. Custom targets fall back to contentBasename. This is a parity gap that the TargetDefinition.fileNameField approach (future WP) will close.

resolveFrontmatterTemplate fallback (frontmatter.ts last line) returns DEFAULT_FRONTMATTER_CLAUDE_CODE for any target that is not 'vscode'. Custom targets will silently receive the Claude Code frontmatter template unless they register a plugin override. This is the known limitation noted by the Developer — a TargetRegistry lookup is the correct fix.

Fix-Forward applied: corrected three JSDoc inaccuracies in src/plugins/types.ts (outVscode @deprecated, outClaudeCode @deprecated, outputDirs) and src/builders/types.ts (targetRegistry). All four fields were documented with runtime claims that do not yet hold — e.g. outputDirs 'When present, supersedes outVscode' and targetRegistry 'When provided, its definitions override the default registry'. Both assertions are false until the follow-up WP wires these fields into the runtime. Corrected to 'Not yet consumed by the runtime / build()' with accurate forward guidance. Changes are JSDoc-only; tsc --noEmit still exits clean.

Documentation-Forward tagged: the precedence comment inside resolveFrontmatterTemplate (frontmatter.ts) is confusing — it says 'last plugin wins (plugins are applied in reverse-registration order)' but the code iterates forward and returns on first match (first registered plugin wins). This comment predates WP-002 but was reviewed as part of the changed file.

comments.note: Corrected @deprecated JSDoc on SuiteConfig.outVscode (src/plugins/types.ts): removed the claim 'outVscode is still read as a fallback when outputDirs is absent' — this implies a runtime precedence chain that does not yet exist. Corrected BuildConfig.targetRegistry JSDoc (src/builders/types.ts): removed 'When provided, its definitions override or extend the default registry' — build() does not yet read config.targetRegistry. Replaced with 'Not yet consumed by build(). Typed now ahead of the follow-up release.'

[documentation-forward] resolveFrontmatterTemplate in src/builders/frontmatter.ts has a contradictory precedence comment: 'the last plugin with a matching key wins (plugins are applied in reverse-registration order so the *first* registered plugin takes precedence)'. The code iterates plugins in forward order and returns on first match — i.e. first registered plugin wins. The comment should be simplified to: 'Plugins are checked in registration order; the first plugin with a matching frontmatterTemplates entry wins.'
